correctness.rationale: On the scalar quadratic, the gradient-sign test is exactly the comparison of \(q_t=\lambda\alpha_t\) with \(1\). The resulting multiplicative map reaches \([1-\beta,1+\beta]\) in finite time, and logarithms conjugate both branches to one rigid rotation. Standard circle-rotation theory supplies the exact periodic/dense dichotomy, while the invariant band gives \(|x_{t+1}|\le\beta|x_t|\).

value.rationale: The method is designed to adapt the learning rate itself. The circle law shows that successful parameter convergence does not imply hyperparameter convergence even on the simplest strongly convex quadratic: the learning rate can be periodic or dense forever. The theorem gives a complete arithmetic classification and explicit diagnostic examples.
